payload.title: Illustrative regulated direct-drive wind turbine

model.title: Illustrative regulated direct-drive wind turbine
model.description: A bounded steady-state teaching model linking wind availability, regulated rotor rotation, generator voltage and resistive-load power. Unqualified proposal for human review.
assumptions: Representative horizontal-axis, direct-drive permanent-magnet generator with an ideal rectifier and a connected resistive load; not a particular product.
All numerical parameters are adjustable-example or fixed teaching assumptions, not measured specifications.
Wind speed defaults to 8 m/s and is restricted to 4–12 m/s. Load resistance defaults to 60 ohm and is restricted to 40–100 ohm.
An ideal, unmodeled aerodynamic regulator maintains tip-speed ratio 4 and adjusts capture to meet shaft demand. Calculated speed is conditional on this assumption, not a prediction from wind alone.
Rotor radius is 2 m; swept area is fixed at 12.566370614359172 m2. Air density is fixed at 1.225 kg/m3.
The averaged rectified generator voltage is proportional to rotational frequency: 31.41592653589793 V at 1 Hz. This is an illustrative generator constant.
Delivered electrical power is 80% of extracted shaft power. The remainder is a lumped conversion loss; this constant efficiency is an assumption, not a fitted efficiency law.

A chosen capture ceiling of 0.30 times available wind power is only an illustrative operating constraint, not an aerodynamic performance curve. Required capture stays below it throughout the allowed ranges.
Each setting represents an established steady operating point. Changes between settings have no modeled acceleration or energy-storage transient.
Rotational-frequency outputs drive actual rotor and shaft rotation. No decorative rotation rate should replace them.
limitations: Aerodynamic lift, blade-force distributions and shaft torque are explained qualitatively, not calculated. This model cannot establish blade geometry or predict a real turbine's operating point.
The ideal regulator is an explicit teaching assumption. Pitch motion, startup, stall, shutdown, overspeed behavior and responses to changing load are not simulated.
Generator voltage is an averaged quantity. Spatial magnetic fields, alternating waveforms, rectifier ripple and electromagnetic torque are not calculated.
There is no product-specific performance, detailed turbulent aerodynamics, structural-load prediction, grid synchronization or validated control-system behavior.
Power is an energy-transfer rate, not accumulated energy. No elapsed-time experiment or energy accumulation is modeled.
Electrical current is calculated, but carrier drift speed and traveling electrical animations are not modeled. Inspection and disassembly do not add physical predictions.

nodes.description: Cycles per second; also drives hub, direct-drive shaft and generator rotor. Range 1.27324–3.81972 Hz.

nodes.description: Rotor frequency divided by the one-Hz reference frequency.

nodes.label: Load voltage
nodes.description: Averaged rectified generator voltage under the assumed linear induction law. Range 40–120 V.

nodes.description: Ohm's law for the connected load; range 0.4–3 A.

nodes.label: Delivered electrical power
nodes.description: Power delivered to the resistive load; range 16–360 W.

nodes.label: Extracted mechanical power
nodes.description: Steady shaft demand including assumed conversion losses; range 20–450 W.

nodes.label: Conversion loss power
nodes.description: Extracted mechanical power minus delivered electrical power; range 4–90 W.

nodes.label: Squared wind speed
nodes.description: Intermediate quantity for wind kinetic-power calculation.

nodes.label: Cubed wind speed
nodes.description: Intermediate quantity for wind kinetic-power calculation.

nodes.label: Density-area product
nodes.description: Air density multiplied by swept area.

nodes.label: Twice available wind power
nodes.description: Intermediate density times area times cubed wind speed.

nodes.label: Available wind power
nodes.description: Undisturbed kinetic-power flux through swept area; approximately 492.60–13300.25 W.

nodes.label: Assumed capture power ceiling
nodes.description: Illustrative capture constraint; approximately 147.78–3990.08 W, not actual extracted power.

nodes.label: Capture headroom
nodes.description: Ceiling minus required shaft power; remains positive, approximately 97.78–3810.08 W.

nodes.label: Required capture fraction
nodes.description: Required shaft power divided by available wind power; approximately 0.01353–0.10150.

snapshot.unfinished_question: How does a wind turbine turn wind into electricity?

definition.title: Inside a direct-drive wind turbine
definition.description: Inspect how blades turn a shaft and generator, then follow the electrical connection to a load. This simplified turbine uses an assumed regulator, not a prediction of real turbine behavior.

limits: Representative direct-drive permanent-magnet generator with an ideal rectifier and resistive load; not a particular product.
Wind speed is 4–12 m/s, default 8; load resistance is 40–100 ohm, default 60. All numerical parameters are teaching assumptions.
Rotor radius is 2 m. The drawing uses 8 scene units per metre; internal component dimensions and the shortened tower are illustrative, not engineering specifications.
An ideal unmodeled regulator maintains tip-speed ratio 4. Load changes alter shaft demand, not regulated speed. No startup, acceleration, pitch motion, stall, shutdown or overspeed is simulated.
Subsequent rotation must use computed rotor_frequency for the shared rotor, blades, shaft and generator rotor. No substitute decorative rotational speed is permitted.
Aerodynamic forces, shaft torque, magnetic fields and opposing electromagnetic torque are qualitative explanations, not calculated fields or forces.
Voltage is an averaged rectified quantity. Alternating waveforms, rectifier ripple, carrier drift and traveling current animations are excluded.

Electrical output is 80% of extracted shaft power; remaining power is lumped conversion loss. The 0.30 capture ceiling is an illustrative constraint, not an aerodynamic performance curve. parts.label: Foundation
parts.explanation: The foundation holds the turbine upright.

parts.label: Tower
parts.explanation: The tower supports the generator above the ground.

parts.label: Machine bed
parts.explanation: This sturdy platform holds the shaft supports and generator.

parts.label: Nacelle cover
parts.explanation: The nacelle is the protective enclosure around the machinery. Remove its cover to look inside.

parts.label: Front bearing support
parts.explanation: This support holds a bearing around the shaft.

parts.label: Front bearing
parts.explanation: Balls between two rings let the shaft turn inside its stationary support.

parts.label: Rear bearing support
parts.explanation: A second support keeps the shaft lined up with the generator.

parts.label: Rear bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the other end of the rotating shaft.

parts.label: Shared rotating assembly
parts.explanation: The blades, shaft and generator rotor turn together without a gearbox.

angular_motion.label: Computed shared rotation shown at one-tenth speed (10× slowdown)

parts.label: Direct-drive shaft
parts.explanation: The shaft carries turning motion from the blades straight to the generator.

parts.label: Blade hub
parts.explanation: The hub joins all three blades to the shaft.

parts.label: Blade one
parts.explanation: Air pushes on the shaped blade, helping turn the hub. The turning effect is called torque.

parts.label: Blade two
parts.explanation: This blade shares the wind's turning effect with the other blades.

parts.label: Blade three
parts.explanation: All three blades turn together around the same shaft.

parts.label: Generator rotor carrier
parts.explanation: This rotating wheel carries the generator magnets.

parts.label: Rotor magnets
parts.explanation: The magnets move past stationary coils. Their changing magnetic influence produces voltage in the coils.

parts.label: Stationary generator ring
parts.explanation: The stator stays still and supports the coils around the rotor.

parts.label: Copper coils
parts.explanation: Voltage is induced in these wire loops. A connected load draws current and creates a magnetic turning effect that opposes the rotor.

parts.label: Generator front plate
parts.explanation: This open plate holds the generator ring in place while leaving room for the shaft.

parts.label: Generator rear cover
parts.explanation: This removable cover protects the back of the generator.

parts.label: Rectifier
parts.explanation: The rectifier makes the generator output flow in one electrical direction. Here its action is idealized.

parts.label: Electrical leads
parts.explanation: Two insulated wires complete the electrical path between the generator electronics and the load.

parts.label: Resistive load
parts.explanation: The load receives electrical power and turns it into heat. Its resistance sets the current for a given voltage.

parts.label: Load terminals
parts.explanation: These two contacts connect the wires to opposite ends of the load.

experiments.title: Wind turns the shared rotor
experiments.prompt: Predict how rotation will change at 10 m/s. Change wind speed, then compare the blades, shaft and rotational-frequency readout.
experiments.explanation: The assumed regulator maintains tip-speed ratio 4, so higher wind speed increases computed rotation. The direct-drive shaft turns the generator rotor at the same frequency. Playback shows this motion at one-tenth speed; acceleration is not modeled.

experiments.title: Inspect the generator
experiments.prompt: Predict the voltage change at 6 m/s. Inspect the magnets beside the stationary coils, change wind speed, then compare voltage.
experiments.explanation: The shaft moves the magnets past stationary coils, inducing voltage. The declared averaged voltage is proportional to rotational frequency; magnetic fields and waveforms are not simulated. Inspection separation is not operating motion.

experiments.title: Connect loading to power demand
experiments.prompt: Predict what lowering resistance to 40 ohm will do to current, electrical power and rotation. Change resistance, then compare the readouts.
experiments.explanation: At fixed wind speed, assumed regulation holds rotation and voltage constant. Lower resistance increases current and delivered power, requiring more shaft power. Loading creates opposing electromagnetic torque qualitatively; torque is not calculated. Electrical power is 80% of shaft power, with the remainder a lumped loss. Power is a transfer rate, not accumulated energy.

controls.help: Wind speed changes available wind power, regulated rotation and generator voltage within this illustrative steady-state model.
Lower resistance increases current and shaft demand; assumed regulation keeps rotation unchanged at fixed wind speed.

coverage.explanation: Computed rotation and power readouts support a partial energy-transfer chain through the direct-drive assembly. Shaft demand includes the assumed conversion loss; aerodynamic capture depends on ideal regulation rather than a predicted blade response.

Inspect blade shape and explain aerodynamic turning forces, then follow shaft motion to magnets passing stationary coils. Explain induction, the connected current path and opposing electromagnetic torque qualitatively; inspection does not simulate forces or magnetic fields.

Wind changes available power, regulated rotation and voltage. Resistance changes current, electrical output and shaft demand, but not regulated speed. All settings are illustrative steady operating points, not product performance or transient predictions.

outcomes: Trace energy transfer from moving air through the blades and rotating shaft to the generator and electrical output.
Explain how aerodynamic forces turn the rotor and how generator motion induces voltage, with electrical current flowing through a connected load.
Explore how wind speed and electrical loading affect available power, rotation and energy transfer within explicitly stated modeling limits.

generation_quality.scope: Recipe, label, connection and dependency checks only. Dependency paths do not prove numeric change. Overlap, recognizability, physical correctness and child usability require separate evaluation.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
